Stated Claim / Post Context:
U.S. police arrest suspect from Washington state in connection with Tumbler Ridge shooting

A 30-year-old allegedly conspired with the shooter to murder people in the B.C. town and broadcast the killings online

Actual Article Body:
Darian and Shelley Quist embrace next to a makeshift memorial on Feb. 12, two days after a deadly mass shooting in Tumbler Ridge, B.C.Jennifer Gauthier/Reuters

A 30-year-old from Washington State was arrested Tuesday and charged with conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country in connection with the February mass shooting in Tumbler Ridge, B.C.

James Cody Bryant, of Bellingham, is alleged to have conspired with Jesse Van Rootselaar to “murder persons in British Columbia, Canada, and then broadcast the killings over the internet for the public to view,” according to U.S. court records.

B.C. RCMP, who have been working with the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation, are continuing their criminal investigation in the province and have signalled the possibility of pursuing further charges in Canada.

This is the first time that authorities in either Canada or the U.S. have revealed that they were pursuing another suspect in relation to the Tumbler Ridge attack.

The arrest is the latest development in one of the deadliest mass shootings in Canadian history, which left eight victims dead, including six children, and devastated the small mining community in northeastern B.C. Its aftermath has been far-reaching, triggering lawsuits, scrutiny of Canada’s firearms oversight and a cross-border reckoning over the lax regulations that govern technology giants when credible threats arise.

Police announce that a 30-year-old from Washington state has been charged with conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country in connection with the February mass shooting that left eight victims dead in Tumbler Ridge, B.C.

Reuters

Law enforcement officials from B.C. and Washington State held a joint news conference in Seattle on Tuesday, where they said the accused is alleged to have provided advice, money and technical assistance to the shooter over the course of six months.

Like the shooter, the alleged conspirator was assigned male at birth and identified as female, authorities said.

Mike Herrington, special agent in charge of the FBI’s Seattle office, said Ms. Bryant “enabled” the shooter and agreed to live-stream the attack to “maximize notoriety.”

“I read a lot of court documents, including some that discuss incredibly heinous acts of violence,” Special Agent Herrington said. “But this complaint was particularly difficult to read, in part because of the casual tone these two individuals used when discussing the mass taking of innocent lives that was being planned.”

The allegations contained within the federal criminal complaint have not been tested in court.

The 18-year-old shooter killed her mother and half-brother at their family home on Feb. 10 before proceeding to Tumbler Ridge Secondary School, where she killed five students and an educational assistant. She then turned a gun on herself.

Remembering the Tumbler Ridge shooting victims: Eight lives lost

According to U.S. court documents, the two are alleged to have tested the quality of the live stream around August, 2025, and in January, 2026. As well, Ms. Bryant is alleged to have given the shooter “tactical advice as to how to carry out the murders,” discussing locations and firearm types that would cause the most damage.

Around Jan. 25, Ms. Bryant allegedly sent $14.33 to the shooter through PayPal for the purchase of a lighter that would be affixed to an explosive device that would be detonated during the murders, the court documents say.

Moments before the shooting began, the accused is alleged to have accessed the live stream. The shooter told her, “I’m going now. Fr. Live. I shot them,” to which Ms. Bryant confirmed to be “watching now.”

Officers believe the two first met on Omegle, a once-popular website that randomly paired users for one-on-one text or video conversations. The website, which shut down in November, 2023, was free to use and did not require an account or registration.

More than 30 pages of messages between the two on Discord are included in court
